summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for Dashboards; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: [low] Billing dashboards contain prebuilt charts that provide insights into Atlas usage. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards.md

[low] The `<Dashboard-Title>.charts` file contains dashboard metadata but does not include certain elements, and exporting a dashboard requires Viewer or higher permissions. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards/dashboard-import-export.md

[low] Dashboards are essential for gaining insight into multiple data focal points in a single display because each individual chart only shows data from a single MongoDB collection or view. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards.md

[low] When importing a dashboard, charts that use a 'Data source in file' are excluded only if you choose the 'Exclude charts using this data source' option. If Atlas Charts detects that a data source in the imported dashboard matches one in the destination project, that data source is selected by default; otherwise Connect later is selected. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards/dashboard-import-export.md

[low] If you choose 'Connect later' for a data source when importing a dashboard, Atlas Charts imports the charts with no data source selected, and they do not render until you edit each chart and choose a new data source. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards/dashboard-import-export.md

[low] Newly created dashboards are not shared by default; only the Owner can view them until access is granted, and the creator automatically holds the immutable Owner permission which cannot be removed or modified. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards/dashboard-access/dashboard-permissions.md
[low] Dashboard export files cannot be larger than 16 MB. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards/dashboard-import-export.md

[low] Atlas Charts displays a warning banner if a user cannot access one or more data sources used on the dashboard, preventing the user from seeing any charts that rely on that inaccessible data source. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards/dashboard-access/dashboard-permissions.md

[low] MongoDB Charts provides a native, zero-ETL way to build charts and dashboards directly from data in MongoDB Atlas, offering real-time dashboarding but with limited customization compared to full BI platforms. Sources: https://hevodata.com/learn/mongodb-visualization/

[low] The dashboard list displays a preview of the first three charts including their titles and types, sorted by default with the most recently modified dashboards appearing first. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards.md
[low] Users can create a new Sample Dashboard even if one already exists by clicking Add and Open, which assigns the creator the Owner role. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards.md

[low] Refresh settings are stored in local browser state and are not persisted with the dashboard or shared between users. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards/dashboard-access/dashboard-permissions.md
[low] Modifying a dashboard's permissions requires the Owner role on that dashboard. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards/dashboard-access/dashboard-permissions.md

[low] A user's own permissions override any permissions derived from the 'Everyone in this project' setting. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards/dashboard-access/dashboard-permissions.md

[low] If an organization uses SSO, MongoDB Cloud prompts users to sign in through the provider to view the dashboard, and these users do not require an Atlas account. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards/dashboard-access/dashboard-permissions.md

[low] Atlas Charts generates a public link that allows anyone to view the dashboard regardless of user permissions. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards/dashboard-access/dashboard-permissions.md

[low] After entering a passcode, the dashboard displays for five days unless the browser session is manually refreshed, after which users must sign in with the passcode again. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards/dashboard-access/dashboard-permissions.md

[low] MongoDB Data Explorer offers quick schema exploration and simple visual queries inside Atlas but supports only basic dashboards, while MongoDB Compass is suited for developers and DBAs needing visual schema views and query debugging but is not ideal for executive dashboards or team collaboration. Sources: https://hevodata.com/learn/mongodb-visualization/
[low] If a dashboard export query takes longer than five minutes, the query times out. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/dashboards/dashboard-import-export.md
